svg.text: VHTR DESIGN PROJECT · MASTER SYSTEMS BOARD · SHEET 1 OF 1
Direct Helium Brayton VHTR — whole-design plate
Target configuration 950 °C, 100 MW(th) reference case. FOAK 850 °C variant overlaid as a ghost throughout. All values traceable to design/00-summary.md.
One fluid, one loop. No intermediate heat exchanger · no secondary working fluid · no water anywhere in the cycle.
RPV ⌀ 5.5 m · core ⌀ 4.6 m · active height 3.0 m · ~200 t IG-110
Each stream changes by exactly 385 K
air-cooled · 215 → 35 °C · no water, no cooling tower

g.text: no gearbox · no oil in the helium

svg.text: WHAT THIS CIRCUIT DOES NOT CONTAIN
A PWR’s secondary side and safety systems are 30–40% of plant cost. Here they
do not exist in any form. That is both the cost argument and the safety argument.

g.text: 11 px ≡ 59 m³/s — turbine exhaust, 600 °C at 1.6 MPa
7 px ≡ 23 m³/s — core inlet, 580 °C at 4 MPa
5 px ≡ 12.6 m³/s — compressor discharge, 195 °C at 4 MPa

svg.text: crossing, no connection · ① state point (T, P) · ṁ = 52 kg/s everywhere
s from s = cp ln(T/T4) − R ln(P/P4), cp = 5,193 J/kg·K, R = 2,077 J/kg·K

g.text: cold stream +385 K ≡ hot stream −385 K

svg.text: Compression 4→5 and expansion 1→2 are drawn between real endpoints, so the
rightward tilt of each is the actual irreversibility (ηc = 0.88, ηt = 0.90).
Peak fuel T is a first-principles resistance sum (§05); design target is < 1,200 °C.
Fit P = 1.8 t−0.346 MW (t in hours) through the §05 values, clamped to 6.5 MW at shutdown.
time after shutdown — hours, log scale (0.01 h = 36 s; 168 h = 1 week)
By the time decay heat falls below what the RCCS removes unaided, the graphite has
absorbed the difference — and nothing at all was asked of an operator.
05 PASSIVE SAFETY — THREE INDEPENDENT MECHANISMS, EACH ON ITS OWN TIMESCALE
hours of buffering — 3.6 × 10⁸ J/°C over 150–250 t of graphite
36 GJ per 100 °C; the core cannot heat quickly even with zero cooling
no pumps, no valves, no power; air is always available

g.text: The three mechanisms overlap in time and none of them can be switched off — each is a material property or a geometry, not a system.

svg.text: Bars: specific capital, $/kW(e), left scale. Line: LCOE, $/MWh, right scale 0–100.
Context: Vogtle AP1000 ~$13,000/kW(e); Hinkley C ~$12,000; APR1400 (UAE) ~$4,500.
The 850 °C FOAK costs $23M less than the 950 °C FOAK and carries no blisk risk.

g.text: shielding mass and security for free
envelope span, at no extra cost

svg.text: one visit a year, in and out
Discharge burnup, GWd/tHM — sweating the fuel
electricity is the mission; H₂ is a load
100 MW(th) core, drawn to scale — the whole plate is one bar wide
an electrical take-off, not a thermal one
S–I thermochemical was rejected: it needs ~850 °C process heat through an intermediate heat exchanger — the
one component this design exists to delete. The nuclear island is identical in both modes; only the load changes.

All values from design/00-summary.md and the linked sections (§03 core, §04 neutronics, §05 thermal-hydraulics, §07 safety, §08 power conversion, §09 hydrogen, §10 fuel cycle, §11 siting, §12 economics). Preliminary design — every number is an estimate awaiting calculation.
